answer: A fishery conservancy registers a signing key only after it takes custody of one numbered oyster cradle on the flats below the navigation knoll. The tide line holds only a hard-capped number of racks without killing the bed, so cradles stay scarce. Enrollment locks a slashable stake equal to the cradle's market lease and records the tag of a living pearl oyster in that rack. Inspectors hoist the cradle, match the tag to the ledger, and require a dye plume from a sealed capsule only the bound key can arm. Every extra fake costs another cradle and another full stake, a linear or worse outlay.
